Jordan Petroleum Refinery Co Reports Strong Financial Results Amid Stable Market Conditions

Jordan Petroleum Refinery Co, the country’s leading oil and gas producer, announced its quarterly financial results on Monday, showcasing a period of steady growth and operational stability. The company reported a net profit of JD 35 million for the first quarter of the year, reflecting a 7% increase compared to the same period last year.

In a statement released to the Amman Stock Exchange, the company attributed its performance to efficient refinery operations and robust demand for petroleum products across the Kingdom. “We are pleased with these results, which are a testament to our ongoing commitment to operational excellence and meeting the energy needs of Jordan,” said Dr. Khaled Al-Masri, Chief Executive Officer of Jordan Petroleum Refinery Co. He added that the company had managed to maintain a stable supply of refined products to all regions, despite global fluctuations in crude oil prices.

Revenues for the quarter reached JD 410 million, supported by strong sales of gasoline, diesel, and jet fuel. The company’s refining throughput remained consistent at 60,000 barrels per day, in line with its production targets. “Our investments in modernizing refinery units over the past year are now bearing fruit,” noted Al-Masri. “This allowed us to improve efficiency and reduce operational costs, which contributed positively to our bottom line.”

Industry analysts welcomed the results, citing the company’s prudent management and favorable market conditions. “Jordan Petroleum Refinery Co continues to demonstrate resilience in a competitive sector,” said Rana Haddad, energy analyst at the Amman Business Review. “With stable domestic demand and enhanced refining capabilities, the outlook for the coming quarters remains positive.”

The company also highlighted its ongoing commitment to environmental standards and sustainability. According to the quarterly report, Jordan Petroleum Refinery Co invested JD 3 million in new emissions control technology, aligning its operations with national and international environmental guidelines.

Union representatives praised the company’s focus on workforce safety and training. “Management has consistently engaged with employees to ensure safe and secure working conditions,” said Ahmad Suleiman, spokesperson for the Jordanian Refinery Workers Union. “This has led to high morale and productivity across the organization.”

Looking ahead, the company reaffirmed its dedication to supporting Jordan’s energy security and economic growth. “We remain focused on delivering value to our shareholders and the people of Jordan,” concluded Al-Masri.
